subject.title: fix(update): dev channel update builds from an unverified checkout at the git install path

question: Should package-to-dev conversion permanently refuse every existing destination, including an empty directory or canonical OpenClaw checkout?
rationale: Fresh cloning is the correct security boundary, but whether existing users must always perform a one-time path move is an operator-facing compatibility policy that correctness evidence cannot decide.

options.title: Approve strict unused-path conversion
options.body: Keep the fail-closed rule, document the one-time operator action, and merge after the Git-template hook path is closed.

options.title: Design an explicit safe takeover flow
options.body: Keep refusal as the default but add a confirmed migration path that proves ownership without adopting existing Git configuration or refs.

options.title: Pause the conversion redesign
options.body: Do not merge until maintainers agree on a compatibility-preserving security model for existing destinations.

recommendation.title: Approve strict unused-path conversion
recommendation.body: Keep the fail-closed rule, document the one-time operator action, and merge after the Git-template hook path is closed.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent work spans the updater handoff and configuration boundary most affected by this policy.
